mainTopic: Lashes without an action: vain and false oaths, תמורה, and cursing with God's name
overview: This amud finishes the reading of 'כי לא ינקה ה'' that רבי יוחנן quoted from רבי מאיר. Only the Heavenly court refuses to clear someone who swore a שבועת שוא, but the earthly court gives him מלקות and that clears him, as אביי proves from the extra word 'ה''. רבי יוחנן then learns from the double 'לשוא' that a שבועת שקר also gets lashes. רבי אבהו asks which false oath this could be, and answers that it is a false oath about the past ('I ate' / 'I did not eat'). רבא explains why: a false oath learned from a vain oath must be about the past, like a vain oath. רבי ירמיה challenges this from a משנה in שבועות. The גמרא shows that the whole משנה follows רבי עקיבא and does not take away lashes from past-tense oaths. רבי יוחנן then removes 'one who makes a תמורה' from the list of sins without an action, because his speech counts as an action. Finally the גמרא learns lashes for cursing one's fellow with God's name from 'והפלא', after showing that a true oath is allowed. It ends by asking whether lashes are really enough for cursing, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Heaven does not clear him, but the earthly court lashes and clears him
steps.stepSummary: The end of the reading of 'כי לא ינקה ה'' that רבי יוחנן gave in the name of רבי מאיר. The Heavenly court does not clear the one who swore in vain, but the earthly court gives him מלקות and that clears him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The Heavenly court] does not clear him, but the earthly court lashes him and clears him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that started before this section. The פסוק says ה׳ will not clear the one who swears in vain, but an earthly בית דין can give him lashes, and that clears him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא ינקה ה'' could sound like 'there is no way out for him.' This reading, in רבי מאיר's name, takes them narrowly: only the Heavenly court refuses to clear him. The earthly court's מלקות does clear him, and this is the source that a שבועת שוא gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The Heavenly court
The earthly (human) court
They give lashes (מלקות)
They clear him, they make him clean of the sin

phrases.english: does not clear him,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started earlier: 'the Heavenly court does not clear him,' read from 'כי לא ינקה ה'' (שמות 20:7).

phrases.english: but the earthly court
lashes him and clears him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל בית דין של מטה מלקין אותו ומנקין אותו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation רבי יוחנן quoted from רבי מאיר, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the Heavenly court does not clear the one who swears in vain (שבועת שוא). The earthly court lashes him, and the lashes clear him.

steps.title: Maybe he can never be cleared at all
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why we don't read the פסוק simply: this sinner has no way to be cleared at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But say that he has no clearing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the reading we just learned. He suggests that 'לא ינקה' plainly means this person can never be cleared, not even by lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain words 'he will not be cleared' sound total. If that is the meaning, there is no source here for lashes, and the earthly-court reading falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Clearing, being made clean of the sin
At all
But let me say (offers a different reading)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא לָא תִּיהְוֵי לֵיהּ נְקִיּוּת כְּלָל!
phrases.english: But say he should have no clearing at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: ואימא לא תיהוי ליה נקיות כלל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that only the Heavenly court refuses to clear him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The simple meaning of 'לא ינקה' is that he is never cleared, so the פסוק may not hint at lashes at all.

steps.title: The extra word 'ה׳' limits the verse to Heaven
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that if the פסוק meant 'never cleared,' it could have just said 'לא ינקה.' The extra word 'ה'' tells us only the Heavenly court does not clear him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, let the פסוק write 'he will not be cleared' and stop. Why do I need 'ה׳'? It is the Heavenly court that does not clear him, but the earthly court lashes and clears him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the reading. He points to the word 'ה'' in the פסוק and says it must be there to limit who refuses to clear him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a reading from an extra word. 'לא ינקה' alone would mean no clearing at all. Adding 'ה'' narrows it: ה׳ does not clear him, which leaves room for the earthly court to clear him through מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reading were right)
And let it be silent, stop there
Why do I need it? (this word looks extra)

steps.whatToRemember: From 'כי לא ינקה ה'': the earthly court gives a שבועת שוא lashes, and the lashes clear him. The word 'ה'' is what limits the 'not cleared' to Heaven.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
let the verse write 'he will not be cleared' and be silent;
why do I need 'ה׳'?

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַעְלָה הוּא דְּאֵין מְנַקִּין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: It is the Heavenly court that does not clear him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל מַטָּה מַלְקִין וּמְנַקִּין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: but the earthly court lashes and clears him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אם כן לכתוב קרא לא ינקה ולישתוק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק limits its meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לא ינקה' means he can never be cleared.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra 'ה'' limits the 'not cleared' to the Heavenly court, so earthly lashes do clear him.

steps.title: We have a source for a vain oath. What about a false oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: we found that a שבועת שוא gets lashes, but where do we learn that a שבועת שקר also gets lashes?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a vain oath. A false oath, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. The source so far covers a שבועת שוא, and now the גמרא looks for a source for a שבועת שקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבועת שוא and a שבועת שקר are two different kinds of oaths. The פסוק 'לא תשא את שם ה' אלקיך לשוא' speaks about שוא. The גמרא wants to know how we extend lashes, even without an action, to a שבועת שקר.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
A vain, pointless oath
A false oath
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found a vain oath;
a false oath, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אשכחן שבועת שוא שבועת שקר מנלן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the finished source for שבועת שוא and asks about a related case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that one who swears a שבועת שקר also gets lashes.

steps.title: The word 'לשוא' appears twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן himself answers: 'לשוא' is written twice in the פסוק. The extra one is not needed for a vain oath, so it teaches that a false oath also gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן himself said: 'In vain,' 'in vain,' twice. If it is not needed for the matter of a vain oath, apply it to the matter of a false oath, that he is lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's own source. He uses the second 'לשוא' in the פסוק for a שבועת שקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'לשוא' already teaches about a שבועת שוא. Since the second one is not needed for that, it is moved to a different topic, a שבועת שקר, and teaches that it also gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Himself (his own view)
If it is not needed for this topic
Apply it to another topic
He gets lashes

steps.confusionAlert: 'אם אינו ענין' does not mean the word has nothing to do with vain oaths. It means the word is extra for that topic, so we use it to teach something new.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan himself said:
'in vain,' 'in vain,' two times;
phrases.notes: שמות 20:7

phrases.english: if it is not needed for the matter of a vain oath,
apply it to the matter of a false oath, that he is lashed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לשוא לשוא שני פעמים אם אינו ענין לשבועת שוא תניהו ענין לשבועת שקר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'לשוא' teaches that a שבועת שקר also gets lashes.

steps.title: Which false oath? Not 'I won't eat' and he ate
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks what case of שבועת שקר this source is for. If he swore not to eat and then ate, he did an action, so no special source should be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו objects: A false oath, what is the case? If we say he said 'that I will not eat' and he ate, there he did an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו starts to attack רבי יוחנן's source. He tests the first possible case and shows it does not need the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of these sources is lashes even without an action. In the case of 'I won't eat' and he ate, eating is an action, so he would get lashes anyway. The extra 'לשוא' would teach nothing new there.

keyTerms.meaning: He attacked it, objected to it
What is the case? How does it look?
If we say
An action

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu objects to it:
A false oath, what are the circumstances?
If we say that he said 'that I will not eat' and he ate,
there he did an action;
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתקיף לה רבי אבהו שבועת שקר היכי דמי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 5 by asking which case it could cover.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of the second 'לשוא' for a שבועת שקר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case involves an action, he gets lashes anyway, so the source teaches nothing new.

steps.title: Nor 'I will eat' and he didn't, since there are no lashes there
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו continues: the other case, 'I will eat' and he didn't eat, has no lashes, since רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rule that one who swore to eat a loaf today and didn't is not lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he said 'that I will eat' and did not eat: is he lashed? But it was stated: 'An oath that I will eat this loaf today,' and the day passed and he did not eat it. רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש say: He is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו finishes his attack by closing off the second possible case. He brings a ruling of רבי יוחנן himself showing there are no lashes there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both cases fail. With 'I won't eat,' he did an action, so the source isn't needed. With 'I will eat,' רבי יוחנן himself says no lashes. So what is the extra 'לשוא' for? Step 8 gives the reasons for that ruling, and step 9 answers the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (trying the other option)
Does he get lashes? (asked in surprise: surely not)
And the day passed

steps.whyThisMatters: The attack is strong because the ruling of no lashes comes from רבי יוחנן himself, the same רבי יוחנן whose source is being attacked.

phrases.english: And rather, where he said 'that I will eat' and did not eat,
is that one lashed?
But wasn't it stated:
'An oath that I will eat this loaf today,'
and the day passed and he did not eat,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say:
He is not lashed.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואלא דאמר שאוכל ולא אכל ההוא מי לקי והאיתמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבי אבהו's attack that began in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's source for lashes for a שבועת שקר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only case without an action ('I will eat' and he didn't) has no lashes according to רבי יוחנן himself, so there is no case left for the source to teach.

steps.title: Why one who swore to eat and didn't is not lashed
steps.stepSummary: This finishes רבי אבהו's challenge. רבי יוחנן says there are no lashes because it is a לאו שאין בו מעשה. ריש לקיש says there are no lashes because the warning is a התראת ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: he is not lashed, because it is a prohibition with no action, and one is not lashed for any prohibition with no action. ריש לקיש says: he is not lashed, because his warning was uncertain, and one is not lashed after any uncertain warning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reasons behind the ruling it quoted in Step 7. Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree there are no lashes when someone swore to eat a loaf today and didn't, but for different reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says not eating is no action at all, and a לאו without an action does not bring lashes. ריש לקיש says nobody can warn him at a clear moment, since until the day ends he could still eat, so the warning is a התראת ספק. Either way, this case cannot be the one that the extra 'לשוא' teaches gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Gets lashes (מלקות)
A Torah prohibition that is broken without doing any action
An uncertain warning: at the time of the warning it is not yet clear that he will actually sin

steps.confusionAlert: Both sages agree on the result (no lashes). They only argue about the reason. Don't think one of them holds he is lashed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he is not lashed,
phrases.notes: This is the case from Step 7: he swore to eat a loaf today and did not eat it.

phrases.english: because it is a prohibition that has no action,
and any prohibition that has no action,
one is not lashed for it.
And Reish Lakish says: he is not lashed,
because his warning was an uncertain warning,
phrases.notes: Until the day is over he can still eat, so there is no clear moment to warn him.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו!
phrases.english: and one is not lashed after any uncertain warning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote begun in Step 7, giving each sage's reasoning.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching (Step 5) that the extra 'לשוא' gives lashes for a שבועת שקר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself rules that the future-oath case without action gets no lashes, so no case of שבועת שקר seems left for his source.

steps.title: The source is for an oath about the past
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that the extra 'לשוא' is about a false oath about the past: 'I ate' when he didn't, or 'I did not eat' when he did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אבהו said: let it be about 'I ate' and 'I did not eat'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו finds a case for רבי יוחנן's source: a false oath about something that already happened. Here the sin is done with words alone, and he still gets lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an oath about the past, the lie happens the moment he speaks, so there is no uncertain warning. Even though no action is done, the special source from the extra 'לשוא' teaches that he is lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier way of thinking and gives a new answer
'I ate': an oath about the past

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Abbahu said:
Let it be about 'I ate' and 'I did not eat'.
phrases.notes: He means: he swore 'I ate' but really didn't, or swore 'I did not eat' but really did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אבהו answers his own challenge from Steps 6-8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a new case for the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the source must be about an oath about the future, and both future cases fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is about a false oath about the past, which is broken by speech alone and still gets lashes.

steps.title: Why is the past different from the future?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why should the פסוק add lashes for 'I ate / I did not eat' and not for 'I will eat' and he didn't? Neither one has an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different, that the פסוק includes 'I ate' and 'I did not eat' more than 'I will eat' and he did not eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי אבהו's answer. If the extra word gives lashes even without an action, why only for the past and not the future?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the person did nothing with his body. So if the פסוק adds a case with no action, the גמרא wants to know why it should be the past oath and not the future one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason for treating two cases differently
Includes: the פסוק adds a case to the rule
'I will eat': an oath about the future

phrases.english: And what is different, that it includes
'I ate' and 'I did not eat'
more than 'I will eat' and he did not eat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רבי אבהו's answer picks the past and not the future.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the extra 'לשוא' includes past false oaths but not future ones, when neither has an action.

steps.title: A false oath is compared to a vain oath
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the Torah made the false oath like the vain oath. A vain oath is always about the past, so the false oath that gets lashes from this source is also about the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the Torah clearly included a false oath that is like a vain oath. Just as a vain oath is about the past, so too the false oath is about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why only the past counts. The false oath is learned from the vain oath, so it must be the same kind of oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for שבועת שקר is the second 'לשוא' in the פסוק of שבועת שוא. Since a שבועת שוא is about something already known (for example, swearing that a stone is gold), the שבועת שקר learned from it must also be about the past.

keyTerms.meaning: Clearly, openly
A false oath
A vain oath, such as swearing about something obviously true or obviously false
About the past

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אבהו and רבא, the lashes for a false oath with no action come from comparing it to a vain oath, so they apply only to an oath about the past.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Torah clearly included
a false oath that is like a vain oath,
phrases.notes: Because it is learned from the extra 'לשוא' in the same פסוק (Step 5).

phrases.english: just as a vain oath is about the past,
so too a false oath is about the past.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The false oath is learned from the vain oath, so like the vain oath it must be about the past.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה quotes a משנה about a future oath
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה challenges רבי אבהו from a משנה. Someone swore three times not to eat a loaf and then ate it, and he is liable only once. The משנה says 'this is' the שבועת ביטוי that gets lashes if done on purpose and a קרבן עולה ויורד if done by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה challenged רבי אבהו: 'An oath that I will not eat this loaf,' 'an oath that I will not eat it,' 'an oath that I will not eat it,' and he ate it: he is liable only once. And this is the שבועת ביטוי, for which one gets lashes if done on purpose and brings a קרבן עולה ויורד if done by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. רבי ירמיה quotes a משנה whose example is an oath about the future, and the next step will show why this is a problem for רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swearing again about the same thing adds nothing, so he is liable only once. The key words are 'וזוהי', 'and this is'. The משנה points to this future-oath case as the oath that brings lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath someone says about himself, to do or not do something, or about what he did
Breaking it on purpose
Breaking it by mistake
Lashes
A 'sliding-scale' offering whose cost depends on how rich or poor the person is

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya challenged Rabbi Abbahu:
phrases.notes: He quotes a משנה from מסכת שבועות.

phrases.english: 'An oath that I will not eat this loaf,'
'An oath that I will not eat it,'
'An oath that I will not eat it,' and he ate it,
he is liable only once.
And this is the oath of utterance,
for which one gets lashes if done on purpose,
and a sliding-scale offering if done by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new challenge against רבי אבהו's answer in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that a past false oath ('I ate / I did not eat') gets lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives a future oath as its example and says 'this is' the oath that gets lashes. The point is finished in Step 13.

steps.title: 'This is' seems to leave out the past oath
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks what the word 'זוהי' leaves out. It seems to leave out 'I ate / I did not eat', teaching that a past oath gets no lashes, which goes against רבי אבהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is': to leave out what? Isn't it to leave out 'I ate' and 'I did not eat', that he is not lashed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה finishes his challenge. He argues that 'this is' means only this kind of oath gets lashes, so the past oath does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word like 'זוהי' limits the rule to the case just mentioned, a future oath not to eat that was broken by eating. The case it seems to leave out is the past oath. That is the opposite of רבי אבהו, who said the past oath is exactly the one that gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is': a word that limits the rule to the case mentioned
To leave out, to exclude a case

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה's case does get lashes because eating is an action. The challenge comes only from the limiting word 'זוהי', not from the case itself.

phrases.english: 'This is': to leave out what?
Isn't it to leave out 'I ate' and 'I did not eat',
that he is not lashed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging conclusion from the משנה quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'זוהי' limits lashes to the future oath broken by an action, which seems to leave out the past oath. That goes directly against רבי אבהו.

steps.title: The word 'this is' only excludes an offering, following רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The word 'זו היא' does not take away lashes from past-tense oaths. It only means that past-tense oaths bring no קרבן when said by mistake, which is the view of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'This is' means: this is the oath where a mistake brings an offering. But for 'I ate' or 'I did not eat', he does not bring an offering. Whose view is this? רבי ישמעאל's, who said a person is liable only for an oath about the future. But he does get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי ירמיה's challenge. The word 'זו היא' leaves out past-tense oaths only from the קרבן, not from lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's sentence has two parts: lashes when done on purpose, and a קרבן when done by mistake. The גמרא says 'זו היא' points at the קרבן part. רבי ישמעאל holds that a קרבן applies only to oaths about the future, but lashes still apply to oaths about the past. So רבי אבהו is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing something by mistake, without knowing it was forbidden
An offering that goes up or down in cost based on what the person can afford; brought for a mistaken oath
The future; an oath about something that will happen
He is given lashes

phrases.english: No, 'this is' the oath for whose mistaken breaking
phrases.notes: The גמרא is rereading the word 'זוהי' from the משנה רבי ירמיה quoted in step 12.

phrases.english: he brings an offering,
but for 'I ate' and 'I did not eat'
he does not bring an offering.
And whose view is this? It is רבי ישמעאל,
who said: one is not liable
except for an oath about the future,
but he does get lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, זוֹ הִיא דְּעַל שִׁגְגָתָהּ מַיְיתֵי קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by changing what 'זוהי' is meant to exclude.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the exclusion and identifying the תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זוהי' excludes past-tense oaths only from a קרבן, following רבי ישמעאל; lashes still apply.

steps.title: The second part of the משנה seems to exclude past-tense oaths from lashes
steps.stepSummary: The second part of the משנה says 'זוהי שבועת שוא', which gets lashes when done on purpose and no קרבן when done by mistake. Here 'זוהי' seems to exclude 'I ate / I did not eat' from lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: 'This is the vain oath, which gets lashes when done on purpose and no offering when done by mistake.' What does 'this is' leave out? Doesn't it leave out 'I ate' and 'I did not eat', meaning he gets no lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבי אבהו from the second part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this part of the משנה the only clear liability is lashes, since a mistake brings nothing. So 'זוהי' seems to mean only this vain oath gets lashes, which would leave out past-tense false oaths. That goes against רבי אבהו.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
A vain oath, like swearing something obviously true or obviously false
Doing something on purpose
To exclude; to leave something out

phrases.english: Say the end of the משנה:
This is the vain oath
for which one gets lashes when done on purpose,
and when done by mistake he is exempt.
What does 'this is' come to leave out?
Isn't it to leave out 'I ate' and 'I did not eat',
that he does not get lashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'what does זוהי exclude' approach as step 13, now on the second part of the משנה, where the step 14 answer does not easily fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's view that a past-tense false oath gets lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second 'זוהי' is only about lashes, so it seems to exclude past-tense oaths from lashes.

steps.title: The second 'this is' only says no offering, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: Here too 'זוהי' is about the קרבן: only the vain oath is exempt from a קרבן, but past-tense false oaths do bring one. That is רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. 'This is' means: this is the oath that is exempt from an offering when done by mistake. But for 'I ate' and 'I did not eat', he does bring an offering. Whose view is this? רבי עקיבא's, who said one brings an offering for an oath about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second 'זוהי' also points at the קרבן, not at lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the vain oath is free of a קרבן. A false oath about the past does bring one, which fits רבי עקיבא. So this part of the משנה also says nothing against lashes for past-tense oaths.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from bringing an offering
About the past

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. In step 14, past-tense oaths bring NO קרבן (רבי ישמעאל). Here they DO bring a קרבן (רבי עקיבא). Notice the switch: that is what the next step attacks.

phrases.english: No, 'this is' the oath that, when done by mistake,
is exempt from an offering,
but for 'I ate' and 'I did not eat'
he does bring an offering.
And whose view is this? It is רבי עקיבא,
who said: one brings an offering for an oath about the past.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, זוֹהִי דְּעַל שִׁגְגָתָהּ פָּטוּר מִקׇּרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 the same way step 14 answered step 13, but it needs a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the exclusion and identifying the תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second 'זוהי' excludes past-tense oaths from lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: It excludes them only from the exemption from a קרבן, following רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: The two halves of the משנה now follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: you said the first part follows רבי ישמעאל, and now the second part follows רבי עקיבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said the first part of the משנה is רבי ישמעאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with its own two answers: they split one משנה between two תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 needed רבי ישמעאל (no קרבן for the past), and step 16 needed רבי עקיבא (a קרבן for the past). One משנה should not be read as switching opinions in the middle without a good reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
But didn't you say? (pointing out a contradiction in what was said)

phrases.english: But you said the first part is רבי ישמעאל!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the combination of the answers in steps 14 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answers in steps 14 and 16 together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Together they split one משנה between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, who disagree on a קרבן for past-tense oaths.

steps.title: The whole משנה is רבי עקיבא, and the first 'this is' excludes 'I will eat'
steps.stepSummary: Since the second part is רבי עקיבא, the first part is also רבי עקיבא. The first 'זו היא' leaves out 'I will eat' when he then didn't eat, not 'I ate / I did not eat'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: since the end is רבי עקיבא, the beginning is also רבי עקיבא. The beginning does not come to leave out 'I ate' and 'I did not eat'. It comes to leave out 'I will eat' when he then did not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for the first part of the משנה, so the whole משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי עקיבא, past-tense oaths do bring a קרבן, so the first 'זו היא' cannot be leaving them out of the קרבן. Instead it leaves out 'I will eat' and he didn't. That case brings a קרבן but gets no lashes, because breaking it involves no action (as in steps 7-8). So past-tense oaths still get lashes, and רבי אבהו stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I will eat' and then he did not eat: an oath about the future broken by doing nothing
Since; from the fact that

steps.whatToRemember: Both 'זוהי's in the משנה follow רבי עקיבא. The first one leaves out 'I will eat and didn't' from lashes. The second one leaves out past-tense oaths from the exemption from a קרבן. Neither one takes away lashes from 'I ate / I did not eat', so רבי אבהו stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the משנה under one תנא and fully answers רבי ירמיה's challenge, so רבי אבהו's source for lashes on a false oath about the past holds up.

phrases.english: Rather, since the end is רבי עקיבא,
the beginning is also רבי עקיבא,
and the beginning does not come to leave out
'I ate' and 'I did not eat',
but rather to leave out 'I will eat' when he then did not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by dropping the רבי ישמעאל reading from step 14 and giving a new exclusion for the first part.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the whole משנה follow one תנא and changing what the first exclusion refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first 'זו היא' leaves out past-tense oaths from a קרבן, following רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה follows רבי עקיבא; the first 'זו היא' leaves out 'I will eat and didn't' from lashes, since there is no action.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ירמיה's proof falls away: past-tense false oaths do get lashes, as רבי אבהו said.

steps.title: Why exclude the future oath specifically?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first 'זו היא' should be read as leaving out the future oath 'I will eat'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about the future oath, that the first part of the משנה leaves it out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the answer from step 18. Why should 'זו היא' leave out 'I will eat' and not 'I ate'? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the גמרא chose which oath the first 'זו היא' leaves out. Now it wants a reason for that choice. Without one, the reading might look random.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Asks for the reason behind a distinction

phrases.english: And what is different?
phrases.notes: He means: why say the first 'זו היא' leaves out the future oath, and not the past one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the reading given in step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first 'זו היא' should leave out a future oath rather than a past oath

steps.title: The clause speaks about the future, so it excludes a future case
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the משנה deals with future oaths, so it makes sense that it leaves out a future case, not a past one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since that part of the משנה is talking about the future, it makes sense that it leaves out a future case. If it is talking about the future, why would it leave out a past case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first part of the משנה is about future oaths. So the word 'זו היא' naturally leaves out a future case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that limits a rule only limits the topic the passage is already talking about. The first part is about future oaths, so 'זו היא' leaves out 'I will eat' when he then did not eat. That is a case where he did no action. So the whole משנה can follow רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: About the future (an oath like 'I will eat')
About the past (an oath like 'I ate')
Leaves out, excludes from a rule

steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה follows רבי עקיבא. The first 'זו היא' leaves out from lashes a future oath that he broke by doing nothing. The second 'זוהי' teaches that only a vain oath brings no קרבן.

phrases.english: Because it is dealing with the future, it excludes a future case;
if it is dealing with the future, would it exclude a past case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause is about future oaths, so its limiting word leaves out a future case

steps.title: Do not list the one who makes a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the תנא to remove 'one who makes a תמורה' from the list of sins that get lashes without an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'and one who makes a substitute': רבי יוחנן told the תנא, 'Do not teach this one, because with his words he did an action.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the list of רבי יוסי הגלילי of sins without an action that still get lashes. רבי יוחנן says the case of תמורה does not belong on that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who makes a תמורה only speaks. But his speech makes a new animal holy. That speech counts as an action, so it is not a sin 'without an action'.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a תמורה, swapping a regular animal for a holy one
Here, the reciter who memorized and taught ברייתות in the study hall
With his speech he did an action

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that speech which changes something's status counts as an action, is the basis of the whole first topic of מסכת תמורה.

phrases.english: "And one who makes a substitute."
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the list of רבי יוסי הגלילי earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to the reciter:
Do not teach "and one who makes a substitute,"
because with his speech he did an action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the list of רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה is not a sin without an action, because his speech makes the animal holy, and that counts as an action

steps.title: Where do we learn lashes for cursing with God's name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that one who curses his fellow with God's name gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who curses his fellow with God's name: where do we learn that he gets lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the list and asks for its source. This sets up the derivation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cursing is only speech, with no action. We usually need a clear source to give lashes for a sin like that.

keyTerms.meaning: One who curses his fellow using God's name
From where do we learn this?

phrases.english: "One who curses his fellow with the Name."
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that cursing with God's name brings lashes

steps.title: 'והפלא' means lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אושעיא, learns the lashes from 'אם לא תשמור… והפלא ה׳ את מכותך'. He reads 'הפלאה' as lashes based on 'והפילו השופט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'If you will not keep… to fear this glorious name,' and right after it says, 'God will make your plagues wondrous (והפלא).' I do not know what this 'הפלאה' is. But another פסוק says, 'The judge shall make him lie down (והפילו) and beat him.' So 'הפלאה' means lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. A person who does not fear God's name, such as one who curses with it, gets 'הפלאה', and that word is shown to mean lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק ties the punishment to not fearing God's name. The word 'והפלא' is unclear by itself. It sounds like 'והפילו' in the פסוק about lashes, so the גמרא reads it as lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'wondrous' punishment in the פסוק, here explained as lashes
Lashes given by a בית דין
You must say, meaning this is the only way to read it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
The verse says: "If you will not keep"
phrases.notes: דברים 28:58. It goes on: '…to fear this glorious and awesome name.'

phrases.english: and it is written: "Then God will make your plagues wondrous."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:59

phrases.english: This 'wondrousness', I do not know what it is;
when it says "And the judge shall make him lie down and beat him before him"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2

phrases.english: you must say: this 'wondrousness' is lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים 'אם לא תשמור' and 'והפלא' teach this, and 'והפלא' means lashes because it sounds like 'והפילו' in the פסוק about lashes

steps.title: Should even a true oath get lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we should not say that even a true oath with God's name gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe even someone who swears a true oath gets lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how wide the source in step 23 is. A true oath also uses God's name, so maybe it should get lashes too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'אם לא תשמור… ליראה את השם' sounds like any use of God's name without enough awe. If so, even an honest oath could seem to fall under it.

keyTerms.meaning: A true oath, where what he swears is correct

phrases.english: Say: even a true oath?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how wide the derivation in step 23 reaches
steps.kashyaTarget: The source from 'אם לא תשמור… ליראה את השם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A true oath also uses God's name, so the פסוק might give lashes for it too

steps.title: The Torah openly allows a true oath
steps.stepSummary: The Torah says openly, 'שבועת ה׳ תהיה בין שניהם', so a true oath is allowed and gets no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written openly: 'The oath of God shall be between the two of them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah itself commands an oath in God's name in a court case. So a true oath cannot be a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah tells a guardian to swear in God's name, a true oath cannot count as not fearing God's name. So the lashes are only for wrong uses of the name, like cursing.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, clearly
An oath in God's name, which the Torah commands in a case with a guardian

steps.whatToRemember: Cursing one's fellow with God's name gets lashes because of 'והפלא', which means lashes. A true oath is allowed, since the Torah itself commands one.

phrases.english: It is written openly:
"The oath of God shall be between the two of them."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:10. This is about a guardian who swears he did not damage his friend's things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: An open פסוק shows the case is allowed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any oath with God's name might get lashes
steps.terutzMaskana: A true oath is commanded by the Torah, so the lashes are only for wrong uses of God's name

steps.title: Maybe the oath only settles the money, but lashes still apply
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק 'שבועת ה׳ תהיה בין שניהם' only lets the שומר clear himself with the owner, but he could still get מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe this only means the oath can settle things with his fellow, but should he still be flogged?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 25. It says maybe the Torah allows the oath only to settle the money claim, but he still gets lashes for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 proved from 'שבועת ה׳ תהיה בין שניהם' that a true oath gets no lashes. The challenge says that פסוק may only show the oath works to clear the שומר with the owner. It may not show that the oath is free of punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: to appease, to settle things with someone
lashes, the punishment of flogging
a person guarding someone else's item, who may have to swear about it

phrases.english: Say that this applies only
phrases.notes: 'This' is the פסוק from step 25, 'שבועת ה׳ תהיה בין שניהם', about the guardian's oath.

phrases.english: to appease his fellow
phrases.notes: He means the oath clears the guardian with the owner, so he does not have to pay.

phrases.english: but should he still be flogged?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְפַיֵּיס אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ, אֲבָל מִילְקָא לִילְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof given in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'שבועת ה׳ תהיה בין שניהם' that a true oath gets no lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק may only make the oath valid for settling money. It does not have to mean the oath carries no punishment.

steps.title: The verse 'by His name you shall swear' shows a true oath is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The Torah commands 'ובשמו תשבע', so a true oath with God's name is fully allowed and cannot bring lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that, because it is written: 'And by His name you shall swear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a true oath cannot bring lashes. The Torah itself tells us to swear by God's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ובשמו תשבע' presents swearing truthfully as something good and allowed. Something the Torah tells you to do cannot be punished with lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and by His name you shall swear', a פסוק showing a true oath is allowed
you cannot say this

phrases.english: You cannot say this
as it is written: "and by His name you shall swear"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: a second פסוק that openly allows a true oath
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A true oath might be valid for money but still punished with lashes
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah commands swearing truthfully by God's name, so there are no lashes for it

steps.title: That verse is needed for רב's rule about swearing to keep מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that 'ובשמו תשבע' is needed for רב's teaching that one may swear to fulfill מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for רב's teaching, as רב גידל said in the name of רב: From where do we know that one may swear to fulfill the מצוות? As it says: 'I have sworn and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous laws.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 27. It says 'ובשמו תשבע' may be teaching a different rule, the one from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב teaches that a person may take an oath to push himself to keep a מצוה. If the פסוק 'ובשמו תשבע' is used for that, it may not be teaching that an ordinary true oath is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed (for a different teaching)
swearing to fulfill the מצוות
from where do we know?

phrases.english: That verse is needed for the teaching of רב
as רב גידל said in the name of רב
From where do we know that one may swear to fulfill the מצוות?
As it says:
"I have sworn and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous laws"
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:106

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'ובשמו תשבע' to prove that a true oath is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already being used for רב's rule, so it may not be free to teach this second rule.

steps.title: Another verse also says 'by His name you shall swear'
steps.stepSummary: There is a second פסוק with the same words, so one can teach רב's rule and the other can teach that a true oath is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another verse is written: 'And to Him you shall cling, and by His name you shall swear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah says 'ובשמו תשבע' twice. That leaves a פסוק free to teach that a true oath is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the same words appear twice, both teachings fit. One פסוק can serve רב's rule and the other shows that a true oath gets no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: another verse
'and to Him you shall cling'

phrases.english: But another verse is written:
"and to Him you shall cling, and by His name you shall swear"
phrases.notes: דברים 10:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 and closes the side discussion
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two separate פסוקים: each one teaches a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one פסוק says 'ובשמו תשבע', and it is used up by רב's rule
steps.terutzMaskana: A second פסוק says the same words, so a true oath is allowed and gets no lashes

steps.title: So 'והפלא' teaches lashes for cursing a fellow with God's name
steps.stepSummary: Since a true oath gets no lashes, the word 'והפלא' must be teaching lashes for cursing one's fellow with God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does it come to teach? It teaches about one who curses his fellow with God's name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main question from step 22. Since 'והפלא' is not about a true oath, it must be about someone who curses his fellow with God's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: True oaths were ruled out in steps 24 to 29. So the lashes learned from 'והפלא' in step 23 now go to מקלל את חבירו בשם.

keyTerms.meaning: what does it come to teach?
one who curses his fellow using God's name

phrases.english: Rather, what does it come to teach?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the word 'והפלא' from step 23, which was read as lashes.

phrases.english: For one who curses his fellow with God's name

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question after the side discussion about true oaths ends
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'והפלא' is the source for lashes for מקלל את חבירו בשם

steps.title: Maybe 'והפלא' is about saying God's name for nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'והפלא' may be teaching lashes for מוציא שם שמים לבטלה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is about one who says the name of Heaven in vain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to read 'והפלא'. Maybe it gives lashes to someone who says God's name for no purpose, and not to someone who curses with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sins use God's name in a wrong way. The challenge asks why we should apply the פסוק to cursing in particular, instead of to the simpler sin of saying the name for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: one who says God's name in vain, for no purpose
but say instead

phrases.english: But say instead
that it is about one who says the name of Heaven in vain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'והפלא' as the source for lashes for מקלל את חבירו בשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק may fit a different sin better, saying God's name in vain, so cursing would have no source.

steps.title: Cursing a fellow is surely no lighter than saying God's name in vain
steps.stepSummary: Even if 'והפלא' is about saying God's name in vain, cursing a fellow with the Name is at least as bad, so it gets lashes too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is one who curses his fellow with God's name any less guilty than one who says the name of Heaven in vain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that it does not matter which sin the פסוק names. Cursing includes saying the name in vain and is even worse, so it gets lashes too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'how much more so' argument. If saying the name for nothing gets lashes, then cursing someone with the name, which is worse, must get lashes as well.

keyTerms.meaning: is it any less (severe)?

phrases.aramaic: מִי גָּרַע מְקַלֵּל אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ בַּשֵּׁם
phrases.english: Is one who curses his fellow with God's name any less guilty
than one who says the name of Heaven in vain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing severity: the worse sin cannot be punished less
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If 'והפלא' is about saying the name in vain, cursing would be left without lashes
steps.terutzMaskana: Cursing is at least as bad, so it surely gets lashes too

steps.title: Maybe cursing is so bad that lashes are not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens its question: cursing is two sins in one, so maybe lashes are too small a punishment to atone for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is difficult for us: say that for one who says the name of Heaven in vain, lashes are enough. But one who curses his fellow with God's name does two wrongs: he says the name of Heaven in vain, and he hurts his fellow. So lashes should not be enough for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what it really meant to ask. Its point is not that cursing is lighter, but that it may be too heavy for lashes to atone for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 32 assumed that a worse sin gets at least the same punishment. Now the גמרא turns that around. The extra harm of hurting a person might mean lashes are not enough of an atonement, so the פסוק of lashes may not apply to cursing at all. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what is difficult for us
it is enough for him
two (wrongs)
he causes pain, he hurts

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mistake this for an argument that cursing is a lighter sin. The גמרא is saying the opposite: cursing may be so serious that lashes cannot atone for it.

phrases.english: This is what is difficult for us:
Say that one who says the name of Heaven in vain
is atoned for well enough with lashes
but one who curses his fellow with God's name
since he does two wrongs
that he says the name of Heaven in vain
and he hurts his fellow
lashes should not be enough for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 32 by explaining what the question in step 31 really meant
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'how much more so' answer of step 32, and with it the use of 'והפלא' for cursing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A worse sin might be too serious for lashes to atone for, so the lashes for the lighter sin would not carry over to cursing.
